text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- Environment and energy minister Svend Auken has not yet decided whether Denmark is to go against the European Commission and follow Austria's example of banning genetically engineered corn.
--- The number of drunken drivers arrested could be tripled if the government implements plans to lower the permitted blood alcohol level from 0.8 to 0.5 percent.

--- The possibility of a European Union court case against Denmark's ban on drinks cans is increasing, following protests from France, Britain and the commission against the ban. Environment and energy minister Svend Auken is to meet Danish environmental EU commissioner Ritt Bjerregaard to discuss the issue.
--- Denmark is to help 11 southern African countries, including South Africa and Zimbabwe, to establish a regional peace-keeping force.

--- In spite of tightened visa demands 6000 foreigners applied for political asylum in Denmark in 1996, the second largest number since 1990 -- not counting 18,000 Bosnians who received temporary residence during the civil war in ex-Yugoslavia.
--- Biotechnology research results are lost due to lack of cooperation between universities and investors, biotechnology researchers say.
